observations.behavior: Adds an explicit task registration name to a Celery shared_task, replacing the implicit module-path-based identity.
observations.posthog_connection: This change preserves message and Beat entry identities after file splitting. Without this pin, queued messages could become unresolvable or duplicate entries could appear, potentially breaking support workflows.

observations.behavior: Explicitly names polling tasks; P1.F2.H1 adds tests checking that all expected named tasks are present.
observations.posthog_connection: Supports reliable scheduling of channel polling without relying on import paths alone, which is relevant when maintaining compatibility across backend refactors.

observations.code_quote: registered = {name for name in app.tasks if name.startswith("products.conversations.backend.tasks.")}
observations.behavior: Adds a test asserting exact set equality between declared task names and those discovered by Celery's loader.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides regression protection against accidental loss of pinned names during future maintenance, supporting operational stability rather than adding new capability.

observations.limitations: All hunks show only naming changes and one small docstring update; no implementation behavior, retry policy, or configuration parameters were altered. The tier relies entirely on metadata preservation.

review.limitations: All hunks show only naming changes and one small docstring update; no implementation behavior, retry policy, or configuration parameters were altered. The tier relies entirely on metadata preservation.
review.reason: Changes preserve existing functionality while preventing identity drift due to module restructuring. This is bounded, localised maintenance with an accompanying correctness check, not a substantive capability improvement.
review.posthog_relevance: Relevant to PostHog’s support and conversation products where queued messages and scheduled jobs depend on stable identities after file splits.
